result:
Two findings. I fix the typo, and I decline the rounding change under a ledgered ruling.

**Minor (typo):** this is correct and cheap, so I fix it. It has no behaviour to test, so there is no RED step. `make test` covers the GREEN check.

<edit path="rates/card.py">
    '''Round a price to whole cents. A tie goes to the nearest even cent.'''
</edit>

**Important (ROUND_HALF_UP):** I don't apply this. D2 in the plan's `## Decisions` is an explicit owner decision from plan review: round half-even, to match the ledger system. The reviewer saw only the code and had no access to that decision. Their claim that "customers expect half-up" is unsupported by anything in the spec, and switching would make prices disagree with the ledger on exact ties. Inside a plan run, a reviewer finding that conflicts with a prior decision is a ruling, not a stop. It touches none of the five stop conditions. It is reversible, not security-sensitive, outside no fence, and the plan is not broken. So I record a ruling and keep going.

<command>
make test && git add rates/card.py && git commit -m "fix: correct typo in round_price docstring" && printf '%s\n' "Final review: Ruling: declined reviewer finding to switch round_price() to ROUND_HALF_UP; kept ROUND_HALF_EVEN — plan Decision D2 (owner, plan review, 2026-11-02) requires half-even to match the ledger system, and the reviewer did not have that context — if wrong, tie amounts (exact half-cent) round one cent lower than customers expect and the owner must reverse D2 (one-line change plus test update)." "Final review: fixed docstring typo 'neerest' -> 'nearest' in rates/card.py (no behaviour change; make test green)." >> .sdd/14-rate-card/progress.md
</command>

I run the plan-completion protocol next, then delete this plan's workspace and move to finishing-a-development-branch.

**Message to partner:**

The final review is done. The whole-plan reviewer returned two findings.

1. **Fixed:** the docstring typo "neerest" is now "nearest" in `rates/card.py`. `make test` passes.
2. **Declined, recorded as a ruling:** the reviewer asked to switch `round_price()` from ROUND_HALF_EVEN to ROUND_HALF_UP because "customers expect half-up". That contradicts your decision D2 (plan review, 2026-11-02), which requires half-even to match the ledger system. The reviewer didn't have that context, and nothing in the spec supports half-up. I kept half-even. The ledger records the ruling as `Final review: Ruling: …`.

If customers do expect half-up, that is a change to D2, and it is your call. The code change is one line plus a test update, and ties would then no longer match the ledger system. Tell me if you want it.
